text:
Ask whether the client has cash flow available for a retirement contribution, whether the contribution is already scheduled, and whether projected income falls inside a synthetic phase-out range. Record the answer before generating an action item.

This intake step keeps cash-flow recommendations separate from credit eligibility recommendations. A client may have capacity to contribute even when the invented credit is phased out, and a client may qualify for a credit but lack cash flow for the contribution.

sectionPath: SYN-TC-4100 Estimated Payment Trigger Rules for Non-Withheld Income > SYN-TC-4100-a General trigger for non-withheld income

citation.documentTitle: SYN-TC-4100 Estimated Payment Trigger Rules for Non-Withheld Income
citation.sectionPath: SYN-TC-4100 Estimated Payment Trigger Rules for Non-Withheld Income > SYN-TC-4100-a General trigger for non-withheld income
citation.syntheticNotice: Synthetic training content; rates and limits are invented.

text:
A covered planning household enters estimated-payment review when it expects material income that is not collected through wage withholding. Non-withheld income includes synthetic dividends, interest, self-employment receipts, consulting fees, concentrated equity proceeds, and similar inflows that are not already covered by scheduled payroll withholding.

The advisor must treat this rule as a planning trigger rather than as an automatic payment command. A trigger means the household needs projection review, source classification, and payment-timing analysis before a recommendation is recorded.

The trigger is intentionally broad so retrieval can distinguish income-source analysis from payment-threshold analysis. A recommendation that asks whether non-withheld income exists should retrieve this provision before it retrieves the safe-harbor table in SYN-TC-4110. A recommendation that already knows the filing status and payment target should retrieve the safe-harbor provision instead.

citation.syntheticNotice: Synthetic training content; rates and limits are invented.

text:
The synthetic review threshold is met when projected non-withheld income exceeds 9,500 for the current planning year or when projected tax due from that income exceeds 1,250 after available credits. Both values are invented training limits.

If both values are below threshold, the advisor may document that estimated-payment review was considered and deferred. If either value is above threshold, the advisor should compare quarterly payment options before the next payment window.

For retrieval testing, this subsection is the expected source when the query mentions material non-withheld income but does not mention a filing status. The invented numbers are deliberately different from the filing-status thresholds in SYN-TC-4110-a and SYN-TC-4110-b so a retriever must attend to context.

citation.syntheticNotice: Synthetic training content; rates and limits are invented.

text:
Income already covered by verified wage withholding does not count toward the non-withheld trigger. One-time reimbursements, corrected payroll deposits, and previously accrued synthetic refunds are excluded unless the advisor documents that they changed the tax projection.

An excluded item may still appear in the case narrative, but it should not drive the estimated-payment trigger by itself. If a client receives both excluded reimbursements and non-withheld consulting income, only the consulting income should be counted for this provision.

citation.syntheticNotice: Synthetic training content; rates and limits are invented.

text:
A household with seasonal synthetic income may use a quarterly exception review when at least 70 percent of the annual non-withheld income is expected in one quarter. The advisor must identify the quarter, the income source, and the payment date used for planning.

This exception does not waive payment analysis. It only permits the advisor to compare payment timing against the season in which the income is expected to arrive.

The exception should be used when the timing of income is the central planning fact. It should not be retrieved first for a general query about dividends, consulting receipts, or non-withheld income unless the query also indicates that income arrives unevenly across quarters.

text:
For synthetic cash contribution planning, the maximum current-year contribution used in the retrieval corpus is 48 percent of invented adjusted planning income. This rule is deliberately similar to SYN-TC-4210-b and differs in contribution limit only.

The 48 percent limit is intended to be easy to confuse with the 52 percent limit. Both sections refer to cash contribution planning, invented adjusted planning income, and substantiation review. The contribution percentage is the only material detail that should separate the two.

text:
The advisor should retain a synthetic support note when projected cash contributions exceed the invented substantiation amount. The support note is training material and is not a real documentation standard.

The support note should identify the source of the projected gift, the expected payment date, and whether the household is also near an itemized deduction cap. It should not invent a real charitable contribution rule.

The synthetic retirement contribution credit begins to phase out when invented adjusted planning income reaches the lower bound shown below. It is fully phased out at the upper bound.

This phase-out provision should be retrieved when a recommendation asks whether income level changes the value of a retirement contribution. It should not be treated as the source for the maximum credit amount after 2026-01-01; that amount is controlled by SYN-TC-4310-b.

citation.syntheticNotice: Synthetic training content; rates and limits are invented.

text:
Within the phase-out range, the advisor should model the credit as gradually reduced. The exact reduction method is outside this corpus and should not be inferred from real tax formulas.

The model should record whether the household is below, inside, or above the invented range. That classification is enough for the corpus and prevents downstream logic from hallucinating a formula not present in the source.

text:
A household outside the phase-out range may still need contribution planning if cash flow or withholding changes. Eligibility review and contribution timing review are separate synthetic concepts.

For example, a household below the phase-out range may still choose to delay a contribution because cash flow is uncertain. That recommendation should cite the playbook for workflow and this provision only if the phase-out status matters.

citation.syntheticNotice: Synthetic training content; rates and limits are invented.

text:
Effective 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31. This superseded synthetic provision allowed a maximum retirement contribution credit of 1,100 for starter households and 1,900 for established households.

Advisors may cite this section only for historical training scenarios dated before 2026-01-01. It must not be used for current-year recommendations once the replacement provision applies.

This section exists to test date-sensitive retrieval. Its topic and language are intentionally close to the replacement provision, but the effective period and credit amounts are different. A scenario date before 2026-01-01 should retrieve this section when the question asks for the old rule.

citation.syntheticNotice: Synthetic training content; rates and limits are invented.

text:
Effective 2026-01-01. This replacement synthetic provision allows a maximum retirement contribution credit of 1,600 for starter households and 2,400 for established households.

Advisors should cite this section for current synthetic retirement-credit planning after the effective date. The replacement updates the invented credit amounts but does not change the phase-out range described in SYN-TC-4300-a.

This section should be paired with SYN-TC-4300-a when a recommendation needs both the maximum credit amount and the income phase-out range. It should be paired with SYN-PB-04-c when the workflow issue is correcting a superseded citation.
